- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate during mean-reversion phases; adjust downward by 1–3% if recent 7–14 day average is higher than forecast.
- Overshoot after volatility spikes; cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak if preceded by >10% price surge.
- Lagged response to true price movements: delay forecast adjustment by 1–3 days if true price rises >5% from prior day.
- Avoid overconfidence in short-term momentum; reduce forecast slope if 30-day history shows no clear trend.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% for 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 5–8% to avoid runaway bias.
- Correct for “forecast drift”: if model consistently overpredicts by 3–5% over 30-day window, apply 3–5% downward bias to next forecast.
